steps.detail: The source describes patterned Au on an elastomeric SEBS film. Thickness and conductor width matter to mechanical response; do not treat one reported test condition as a universal product specification.
steps.check: Evaluate continuity and resistance on a flat witness sample before rolling. Exact metal deposition setup requires qualification.

steps.title: Release and roll
steps.detail: Rolling the composite changes cross-section and contact accessibility. Keep a carrier handling fixture distinct from a thermal fibre draw tower.
steps.check: Inspect outside diameter, visible site openings and any damage at film edges.

steps.title: Separate magnetic hardware from the passive coupon
steps.detail: The original design includes an optional magnetic-guidance implementation. The actuation, tracking and external magnetic guidance apparatus are outside this workbench profile.
steps.check: Do not label a passive electrical coupon a movable system or infer magnetic behavior from trace continuity.

steps.title: Map electrical retention under strain
steps.detail: Compare resistance on each flat path to the same rolled path. In an inert mechanical fixture, repeated strain can affect both interfaces and conductor integrity.
steps.check: One failed conductor changes one net, not the number of originally patterned sites.

gaps: Specific film transfer tools, precise roll geometry, connector design and magnetic subsystem remain unqualified. No in vivo movement or therapeutic claims are made.

sources.title: Nature: A movable long-term implantable soft microfibre (2025)
sources.note: Fabrication / extended Fig. 1: composite film, rolling, trace-width and thickness tests, 60-channel reference.

profiles.title: SINANO | 16-channel all-hydrogel fibre array
profiles.summary: The reported microscale conductor is a PEDOT:PSS hydrogel fibre shaped by wet spinning, stretching and annealing. The observable result depends on hydration and load, not just a dry fibre diameter.

variants.label: Published 16-channel array
variants.description: The paper reports controllable 1–20 µm conductor diameter and a 16-channel assembly. That range is not a list of separately validated complete 16-channel configurations.

variants.label: Single-fibre witness
variants.description: A witness fibre isolates hydration-dependent diameter and electrical behavior; it has no multichannel routing.

steps.title: Keep the three objects distinct
steps.detail: Model fibre formation, interface insulation/support and multicontact fanout as distinct components. Geometric fibre diameter does not specify contact area, electrical channel count or exact pad routing.
steps.check: Compare a single observed fibre and the 16-channel assembly without equating them.

steps.title: Obtain qualified spun, stretched fibre
steps.detail: The authors coordinate spinning, elongation and annealing of conductive hydrogel fibres. A syringe pump offers only a feed subsystem: the register has no qualified take-up/stretch/anneal line for this process.
steps.check: Do not assign an electrospinner simply because the article calls its process spinning.

steps.title: Compare conditioned witness sections
steps.detail: Hold a documented hydration state for diameter comparisons. Short sections and representative longitudinal micrographs serve different measurements.
steps.check: Separate hydrated optical observations from dried vacuum micrographs; use the same state for control/comparison.

steps.title: Assemble and map the breakout
steps.detail: The published array has 16 channels. A bench surrogate needs an explicit interface map, intact insulation and protected contact transitions. Exact package and termination tooling are not assumed.
steps.check: Sixteen conductors in view are not sixteen independently tested outputs.

steps.title: Measure conduction and mechanics
steps.detail: For a named hydration state, compare electrical continuity/impedance and flex response on nonliving samples; repeat after conditioning.
steps.check: If the terminal resistance dominates or several fibres share a return, report that ambiguity rather than a bulk material property.

gaps: The exact process line, per-fibre connector mapping, manufacturing yield and direct equivalence of dry and wet fibre dimensions remain unavailable here.

sources.title: Wang et al., Matter: neuron-scale all-hydrogel array
sources.note: 2026 primary report: PEDOT:PSS fibre, stretched/annealed construction, 1–20 µm range and the 16-channel architecture.

profiles.title: Fudan | susceptibility-matched PEDOT:PSS fibre coupon
profiles.summary: Here the conducting core is wet-spun PEDOT:PSS, and the jacket is PDMS. A reduced magnetic-susceptibility artifact in a particular experiment is not a general MRI-safety label.

variants.label: Reported insulated fibre
variants.description: The primary paper illustrates an approximately 15 µm PEDOT:PSS core and a PDMS insulating layer; electrochemical results must retain their specimen diameter and exposed length.

variants.label: Passive MRI comparison
variants.description: A nonliving geometry fixture compares artifacts only under the stated field, orientation and sequence; not an MR Conditional system claim.

steps.title: Obtain wet-spun fibre
steps.detail: The source describes wet spinning followed by conditioning to alter the fibre structure/flexibility. An exact wet-spinning/take-up system rather than an electrospinner is required.
steps.check: Record conductor identity and the conditioning state independently of downstream silicone insulation.

steps.title: Add jacket and expose chosen region
steps.detail: PDMS insulates the core along its shaft; exposed conductor differs from the total visible fibre. An optical witness section is useful to distinguish surface exposure from metal-like shine.
steps.check: Measure exposed geometry, shaft isolation and resistance separately.

steps.title: Characterize electrical interface
steps.detail: Use inert electrolyte and reference/counter electrodes to compare impedance with the cited specimen. Electrode length, diameter and frequency must accompany any impedance number.
steps.check: Do not apply a 20 µm specimen measurement to a 15 µm specimen as if geometry were unchanged.

steps.title: Separate the MRI comparison from safety
steps.detail: The paper reports experiments up to 11.7 T. The register’s 7 T scanner is not the source’s 11.7 T experiment. A passive phantom can examine artifact under a specified local sequence only.
steps.check: No field-strength equivalence, heating, safety label, or patient inference follows from a small image artifact.

gaps: Supplier-grade fibre formation, terminal sealing, matched phantom conditions, source field/coil/sequence and full system MRI behavior are unqualified.

sources.title: Li et al., MRI-compatible soft fibre bioelectronics
sources.note: Fabrication and MRI compatibility / Fig. 2: wet-spun PEDOT:PSS, PDMS insulation, comparison of imaging artifacts. Research results only.
